protocol.selection_order: All scope exclusions by registry_order, then all exceptions by counselor_programme_id; resume by audit_population plus counselor_programme_id.
protocol.population_start: Current normalized data/registry/programmes.csv; upstream DUO/RIO population is out of scope.
protocol.confirmed_meaning: Supports only the facts and decision within audit_scope. For no-defensible-ucr-match, confirmation applies only to external-programme basis; UCR reassessment remains pending.
protocol.outdated_rule: Requires dated evidence establishing that the original decision was supportable and that a later change superseded it. Record temporal uncertainty explicitly when historical evidence cannot distinguish incorrect from outdated.
protocol.resolved_external_curriculum_action: Normally reassess-exception: an externally reconstructable comparator alone does not establish UCR feasibility.
protocol.reprocess_as_comparison_rule: Recommend only when comparison eligibility is independently established; do not infer it merely from resolved external evidence.
protocol.incomplete_batches: Keep pending cases explicit without audit_finding; never count pending cases as audited.
protocol.final_reconciliation: Every excluded target and every current exception must have exactly one completed audit entry per audit_population; report missing in-scope records separately.

reconciliation_evidence.exception_type_check: Read all 140 exception canonical JSON records directly; verified their IDs and recordStatus and inventoried exception.type only. This is population enumeration, not exception research.
reconciliation_evidence.comparison_count_basis: Current generated review index, with its complete ID set reconciled to both registry scope and canonical filenames; comparison contents were not audited.

Lab/synthesis, analysis, quantum/physical/organic/inorganic chemistry and chemical safety are substantive requirements. Project requires first year plus 130 EC and approval steps. Minor choices are deepening Chemistry, Industrial Chemistry or university minors. Table visually inspected.

Required process-engineering core includes reactors, transport, thermodynamics, separations, process control/equipment, polymer analysis/engineering practicals, Process Design 10 and research 15. Electives may come from bachelor programmes with individual approval; five listed chemical-engineering options are examples, not a licence to treat optional Polymer Engineering as an extra requirement. The PDF repeatedly says 2025/2026, while the official index links this exact file as 2026–2027. Keep that source conflict explicit. rug_astronomy_ter_b7.title: TER appendix BSc Astronomy 2026–2027
rug_astronomy_ter_b7.fact: Mandatory Astronomy major 150 plus free minor 30. First and second years each total 60; final major is Advanced Electrodynamics 5, Astrophysical Hydrodynamics 5, Interstellar Medium 5 and research 15. Mathematics, general physics, observations, computing and astronomical research establish the core. The two 30-EC deepening minors are optional ways to fill minor space; the 15-EC university minor Astronomy through space and time is explicitly unavailable to Astronomy/Physics/Applied Physics students. The selected generic 30-EC minor therefore remains valid without inventing a named minor. Current appendix differs from the older public summary (Mathematical Physics/Cosmology); stored components follow the current appendix. Table visually inspected.

rug_linguistics_oer_b7.title: OER Taalwetenschap 2026–2027
rug_linguistics_oer_b7.fact: Adopted 7 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026. September 2026 ordinary route: first year 60, second year 60 including Morphology 5, Statistics 5 and Psycholinguistics Project 10, minor 30 and three of five graduation-portfolio units at 10 each. First three formally listed portfolios are Neurolinguistics, Psycholinguistics/Developmental Language Disorders and Syntax. Speech-Therapy minor participants have specific second-year exemptions and mandatory portfolio selections; those are not the selected ordinary pathway. A standalone extra thesis is not prescribed beyond the graduation portfolio. Current webpage’s older second-year list differs; formal cohort table controls. Table and footnotes visually inspected.

rug_dentistry_oer_b7.fact: Adopted 20 May 2026. Ordinary Dutch/full-time programme has no tracks, minor space or elective components. All 29 units total 60+60+60=180. Third year includes professional skills 12, scientific skills/research 8, supervised Bachelor Clinic 12 and other oral-health/diagnosis/radiation-protection/context study. Clinic entry requires completed first year, both second-year professional-skills units, oral-healthcare context 2, three of four theory units and scientific skills 2. rug_dentistry_prospectus_b7.title: Tandheelkunde
rug_dentistry_prospectus_b7.fact: Dutch/full-time 180-EC bachelor, 56560. Bachelor research/thesis is completed alongside the clinical sequence. The full professional qualification includes a subsequent three-year master, so bachelor clinical formation is not itself a claim of completed dentist licensure.

rug_iem_ter_b7.title: TER appendix BSc Industrial Engineering and Management 2026–2027
rug_iem_ter_b7.fact: First year 60; common upper-year core 30; one specialisation 40; minor 30; integration project 20, total 180. rug_applied_physics_ter_b7.title: TER appendix BSc Applied Physics 2026–2027
rug_applied_physics_ter_b7.fact: One Applied Physics major and a deepening Applied Physics minor, not generic free-minor space. Current tables give 60+60+60=180. Four laboratory/design units are compulsory. Final year has six compulsory 5-EC technical units, three restricted choices of 5 each and research 15. Selected Atoms and Molecules, Principles of Measurement Systems and Nanoprobing/Nanofabrication are first in their distinct groups. rug_applied_math_ter_b7.fact: Selected ordinary route is major 165 plus minor 15, total 180: first year 60 and later major requirements 105. Project Mathematical Modelling/Systems Theory and Numerical Linear Algebra/Advanced Systems Theory are the first available selections in two distinct choose-two groups. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Radboud degree is an integrated molecular biology AND chemistry programme. Its compulsory first year already includes atoms and molecules, analytical chemistry and a chemical-analysis lab, organic chemistry and synthesis lab, biochemistry and its lab, thermodynamics, cell biophysics and a molecular-sciences lab. The later compulsory core deepens organic, inorganic and analytical chemistry, crystal structure, biomolecular mechanisms and structural bioinformatics, then requires a supervised 12-EC research internship. UCR offers valuable molecular-cell and biomedical courses but lacks a sequence in organic/inorganic/analytical/physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and synthesis, and has only one broad life-science laboratory course. A 24-course UCR schedule could sustain biomedical biology with data methods, but it would omit the defining chemistry and multi-lab spine and would misrepresent equivalence to this molecular-science degree.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: VU's current official pages (checked 2026-09-27) confirm a 180-EC, three-year Bachelor Theologie en Religiewetenschappen offered voltijd and deeltijd, with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen selected from year 1 (Theologie, Islam, and the selected Religie en Levensbeschouwing/Zingeving route); the deeltijd variant carries the identical 180-EC curriculum at a reduced pace rather than a distinct credit structure. The selected route's own page names its year-by-year course themes -- the origin of religious traditions, world religions and conflict/peacebuilding in year 1; meaning-making/mental health and religion and trauma in year 2; a flexible-location minor plus a scriptieseminar-and-bachelorscriptie and electives such as philosophy of religion in year 3 -- but supplies no EC, compulsory-status or credit-table information for any of them. provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The normalized target (cp-000119, registry row 127, canonical_name 'B Theology and Religious Studies (deeltijd, Nederlands)', source_provider_id 111A136, programme_unit_code 1001O5760, recognized_programme_code 50910, languages_json=["NLD"], modes_json=["DEELTIJD"]) names no specific route. VU's current official overview page (s0, checked 2026-09-27) confirms a 180-EC, three-year bachelor offered '3 jaar Voltijd en deeltijd' with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1: Christelijke theologie (Theologie), Islamitische theologie (Islam, which s0 itself describes as 'the only Islamic-theological WO bachelor in the Netherlands'), and Religie en Levensbeschouwing (also branded 'Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving'); s4, a third-party study-choice aggregator republishing VU's own submitted programme data, independently confirms the 180-ECTS total and the same three afstudeerrichtingen. Applying the Section 2.1 neutral route-selection hierarchy (the target is generic and no route is clearly more representative): the Theologie track's own current page (s2) requires a compulsory Hebrew (Hebreeuws I-III) and Greek (Greek I-III + New Testament) biblical-language sequence and offers tradition-specific confessional seminary sub-tracks (Hersteld Hervormd, Baptist, Mennonite); the Islam track requires compulsory Arabic-language study and Qur'an/hadith/fiqh confessional training (s0; independently corroborated by generator-eligible programme-interest rows 5410, 5411, 5412, 5413 naming Qur'an/hadith exegesis, Sharia jurisprudence and Arabic-language study as structural Islam-track content). Religie en Levensbeschouwing is instead described by its own current page (s1) as an explicitly comparative, multireligious, 'dialogisch' course of study engaging several religious traditions rather than forming students within one confessional tradition, with no compulsory classical/liturgical-language sequence. It is therefore the least specialized/most general of the three formal routes and is selected as the reconstructed route. However, s0, s1 and s2 give only qualitative year-by-year course-name lists for their respective tracks (for the selected route: year 1 covers the origin of religious traditions and world religions plus 'Conflict and Peacebuilding'; year 2 covers 'Zingeving, religie en mentale gezondheid' and 'Religie en trauma'; year 3 includes a flexible-location minor, 'Scriptieseminar en bachelorscriptie', and electives such as 'Godsdienstfilosofie') without any EC weight, compulsory-versus-elective status, or credit table for a single component. VU's own current regulations page (s3, checked 2026-09-27) states that the formal Teaching and Examination Regulations for every VU programme are 'published in the Study Guide' at studiegids.vu.nl; that portal's landing page carries only top-level dynamic category navigation with no extractable curriculum content, and a constructed direct URL for this exact study guide entry returned HTTP 404 to available retrieval tools, matching the same dynamic-portal limitation already documented for another current VU counselor target (cp-000118). Reasonable further search located only one standalone official OER PDF for a VU theology bachelor, 'Onderwijs- en Examenregeling Bacheloropleiding Theologie 2017-2018' (s5); its own text shows 'Minor Islam' offered only as one elective minor within a single undifferentiated Theologie bachelor, not as one of three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1, so it predates and does not reliably describe the current three-route structure and is preserved only as evidence of how substantially the formal structure has since changed, not used to supply component credits. No third-party source (s4; the Qompas study-choice listing checked during research) publishes a per-course EC table either. Because no accessible current or formally adopted source establishes exact EC weights, compulsory/elective status or a stable component list for the selected route, no 180-EC component list is supplied.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum of the selected route is a chemical-engineering sequence built on physics and chemistry: Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, and Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics in the compulsory first year, physics, electronics, chemistry and biology laboratory skills, fluid mechanics and heat and mass transfer in year 2, and in year 3 chemical engineering thermodynamics and kinetics, separation processes, reactor engineering, chemical plant design, process design and control, unit-operations and industrial-process-design skills and a 25-EC engineering thesis. UCR offers circular-economy, life-cycle, energy and environmental-engineering-adjacent courses, a mathematics and numerical-methods line and biochemistry and cell-biology courses, but no physics, chemistry sequence, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactor or process engineering, mechanics or engineering design. A 24-course programme would be a sustainability-and-mathematics programme with a small circular-economy core padded with unrelated life-science or computing courses, and it would not reproduce the programme's engineering substance; the unmatched components include essentially all of the 25-EC concentration course sequence, the engineering physics and chemistry core and the thesis. The comparison would have to present adjacent sustainability courses as substitutes for engineering content that UCR does not teach.

provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026-2027 (Education and Examination Regulations BSc Circular Engineering, Faculty of Science and Engineering, in force 1 September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-03)
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The programme pages (s1, s2) describe the structure in words only: a common first year, a second year of electives, skills and projects, and a third year with one of four concentrations and a thesis; they give no course list with EC. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s0): Article 3.6 (study load per year), 3.7 (core), 3.8 (electives), 3.9 (concentration and thesis) and Appendix I (course overview). Year 1: eight mandatory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of skills courses and two 5-EC projects. Year 2: eight elective 5-EC courses and four elective 2.5-EC skills courses (two courses and one skill per period, chosen from the published framework) plus two mandatory 5-EC projects; the framework is availability-dependent, so one coherent valid selection linked to the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration is instantiated (Organic Chemistry, Fluid Mechanics, Numerical Methods, Polymeric Materials, Differential Equations, Biochemistry, Heat & Mass Transfer, Remake Reuse Repair Recycle; skills in organic chemistry, statistics, fabrication and design, and analytical and physical chemistry) and is flagged here as an instantiation of restricted choice rather than a fixed requirement. The Heat & Mass Transfer elective is explicitly linked to this concentration, which satisfies the requirement that one elective be linked to a third-year concentration. Year 3: one mandatory 5-EC core course (Ethical and Philosophical Reflections), the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration of five 5-EC courses (the fifth, Circular Process Design and Control, shown in the period 3-4 slot) and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC bachelor thesis (BTH3010). cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Groningen explicitly defines Industrial Engineering and Management as a predominantly technical engineering degree: two-thirds technical science and one-third business. The selected pathway combines calculus, linear algebra, statistics, programming, materials and transport phenomena with engineering-system dynamics, complex-system design, mechanics, signals, control, CAD and manufacturing, production techniques, construction, mechanical craftsmanship and a 20-ECTS industrial integration project. UCR can reproduce meaningful business, data, programming, mathematics, sustainability and product-design context, but it has no coherent mechanics, materials, transport, manufacturing, control-engineering, construction or workshop sequence and no comparable industrial-engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore shift the degree's centre of gravity from engineering to general business and data study rather than constitute a defensible closest match.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The formally published 2026-2027 programme appendix establishes a complete 180-ECTS pathway: 60 ECTS of compulsory first-year courses; a 30-ECTS common IEM core across Years 2-3; a 40-ECTS specialisation; 30 ECTS of genuine minor space; and the 20-ECTS Bachelor Integration Project. The generic normalized target requires one of two equal 40-ECTS specialisations. Neither is formally presented as more representative, so Production Technology and Logistics is selected by the official-order tie-break. The minor space remains open rather than being populated with invented courses. The current programme page independently describes the degree as two-thirds technical science and one-third business, with training in mathematical and physical modelling, production, logistics, sustainability, management and technical/economic feasibility.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Applied Physics is a cumulative experimental and engineering-physics degree. Its compulsory formation progresses through mechanics and relativity, electromagnetism, quantum and thermal physics, waves and optics, atomic and solid-state physics, fluid physics, materials science, electronics, signal processing, device physics, control engineering, instrumentation and nanofabrication. Four staged laboratory/design components and a 15-ECTS Applied Physics research project integrate that disciplinary sequence. UCR provides useful mathematics, programming, data, robotics and sustainable-energy applications, but no disciplinary physics sequence, experimental-physics laboratories, materials/device/instrumentation formation or physics research capstone. A UCR programme assembled from quantitative and adjacent technology courses would not be a defensible Applied Physics comparator.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Groningen bachelor is a full disciplinary Applied Mathematics degree. Its 165-ECTS major builds from proof-based analysis, calculus, sets and numbers, graph theory, two linear-algebra courses, probability, programming, mechanics and linear systems into topology, complex and functional analysis, multivariable analysis, ordinary and partial differential equations, numerical analysis, optimization, mathematical modelling, computational science, advanced systems and modelling projects, and a 15-ECTS Applied Mathematics research project. UCR offers a useful six-course mathematics sequence plus programming, data science and selected computational applications, but it does not provide the breadth, depth or staged project and research spine required for a 24-course Applied Mathematics programme. A UCR programme assembled from mathematics, AI, data science and applications would be a coherent quantitative or computational pathway, not a defensible substitute for the target degree.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 165-ECTS Applied Mathematics major and 15-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation. The remaining 120 ECTS comprise 105 ECTS of major requirements and 15 ECTS of genuine minor space. First-year Project Applied Mathematics is used because it directly represents the named degree. For the two required project choices, Project Mathematical Modelling and Project Systems Theory are selected as the first two options in official order. Numerical Linear Algebra and Advanced Systems Theory are likewise the first two options in the required advanced-choice group. Statistical Modelling is the first Applied Mathematics elective not already used. These choices are fixed independently of UCR fit, and the open minor remains unpopulated.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods covers foundational calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and introductory linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics extend that base. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving. The workbook also contains relevant content in DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISARIN211 Decision-making in AI, DISCOMP311 Algorithms & Data Structures, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics. However, the available curriculum has no dedicated proof-based sequence in real analysis, metric and topological spaces, complex analysis and functional analysis; no full sequence in ordinary and partial differential equations; no graph theory, sets and numbers, advanced systems theory or multiple applied-mathematics modelling projects; and no equivalent 15-ECTS disciplinary research project. Several especially relevant courses, including DISMATH213, DISMATH312 and DISDATA312, have no planned term for the Fall 2026 cohort in the authoritative workbook. These gaps prevent an academically honest 24-course Applied Mathematics closest match.
